newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma grabs for privatisation control.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma grabs for privatisation control.

text.p: The Russian Duma lower parliament house on Tuesday widened its control over privatisation by sending a law requiring the government to seek approval of privatisation targets to the upper chamber.
The Duma approving in a third, final reading the draft law which must be approved by the Federation Council upper house of parliament and then by President Boris Yeltsin to become law.
A total of 311 deputies of the communist-dominated Duma voted for the law and only nine were against.
The law would require the cabinet to present lists of companies to be sold to parliament for approval.
It also calls for investors to provide certain social protection for employees at of privatised enterprises and introduces a number of fines for delayed payments and unfulfilled terms of sell-offs.
The draft law makes the Russian rouble the sole legal tender in the course of sell-offs.

Millions of dollars of state property changed hands in Russia's historic sell-off drive in 1992-1996, spearheaded by young reformer Anatoly Chubais, who is now Russia's First Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister.
The communist-nationalist majority in the Duma earlier this month called privatisation unsatisfactory in a resolution which said the sell-offs broke the law in many cases.
Deputies blamed Chubais for selling Russia's riches cheaply and for opening up the country to criminals and speculators.
The new law, they say, is supposed to bring more order into the privatisation scheme.
